newsitem.title: FRANCE: Family to sue after suicide over child abuse probe.
newsitem.headline: Family to sue after suicide over child abuse probe.

text.p: The family of a teacher who committed suicide after he was targeted in a crackdown on child sex abuse announced a lawsuit on Sunday accusing investigators of dragging his name through the mud.

Gilbert Pic, 39, threw himself from a bridge into the river Garonne in the southwestern city of Bordeaux on Saturday, the fourth man to commit suicide amid a French blitz against suspected paedophiles. His body has not been found.
Lawyer Benoit Ducos-Ader said he would file a suit on behalf of Pic's family accusing magistrates of "endangering his life" and alleging violations of judicial secrecy.

"When magistrates use the press to puff themselves up, I think it neither honours justice nor the press," he told La Chaine Info television. The suit would let relatives find out "how his name was dragged through the mud."
Pic had been placed under examination by a magistrate on Friday on suspicion of corrupting minors and handling pornographic pictures of minors.

His case was not directly linked to an unprecedented string of police raids since Tuesday on hundreds of people, most of them suspected clients of a firm selling videos featuring sexual abuse of minors.
A total of 323 people have been placed under investigation and 24 people are in detention.

Catherine Trautmann, spokeswoman for the new Socialist-led government, said she did not believe the number of paedophile crimes in France was on the rise but that taboos hushing up such offences had been broken.
France now had to "avoid a double reef of the silence that means people don't know, and of spectacle to ensure we don't add to the tragedy," she told TF1 television.

TF1 also quoted the prosecutor leading the hunt into the sex videos, Jean-Louis Coste, as calling the suicides regrettable. But it said he also asked who the police were really meant to be protecting in France.
No one has yet been tried. Being placed under investigation in France is short of an indictment but is often a first step towards a trial.
Some 2,500 police were involved in the raids, which have ensnared teachers and clergymen on the mailing list of a company in the central city of Macon.

Police believe the suspected ringleader, Bernard Alapetite, copied foreign child sex videos -- featuring rapes of boys aged under 15 and even sex with animals -- and sold them for 800 francs ($140) each.
